Container.Name: WinBox
Container.Overview: Windows in a box with an NVIDIA GPU: Windows 10/11 (or Server) in a QEMU/KVM virtual machine inside a container, using an NVIDIA card that stays shared with Unraid and your other containers (Plex, Jellyfin, AI apps). Windows gets DirectX 11 on the GPU through the experimental Triton driver, and Moonlight streaming with the video encoded on the GPU (Sunshine with NVENC, CUDA 12) inside the container. Installs itself automatically on first start; watch progress in the WebUI. Also: persistent storage on your array or cache, an Unraid share as drive Z:, optional dedicated VFIO passthrough, and USB passthrough. See the project README for setup.
Container.Requires: Hardware virtualization (Intel VT-x or AMD-V) enabled in the BIOS. Unraid 7.3 or newer. For DirectX on a shared Nvidia card: the Nvidia Driver plugin with modesetting on, and the Triton driver inside Windows (see README). --memory in Extra Parameters caps the whole container; keep it about 8G above RAM. Without an Nvidia GPU, remove --runtime=nvidia and the two /usr/lib64 mounts from Extra Parameters.

Config.Name: Web console
Config.Description: Browser console, used to watch the installation.

Config.Name: RDP (TCP)
Config.Description: Remote Desktop. Sign in with the username and password below.

Config.Name: RDP (UDP)
Config.Description: Remote Desktop over UDP, smoother video.

Config.Name: Windows storage
Config.Description: Holds the Windows system disk image. Use the pool path (/mnt/cache/... or /mnt/<pool>/...), not /mnt/user/..., which adds a slow FUSE layer.

Config.Name: Shared folder (Z:)
Config.Description: An Unraid share that shows up in Windows as the 'Shared' desktop folder and drive Z:.

Config.Name: Second disk storage
Config.Description: Optional. Folder for a second virtual disk, used together with 'Second disk size'.

Config.Name: Second disk size
Config.Description: Optional. Size of a second virtual disk, for example 500G. Needs 'Second disk storage'.

Config.Name: Custom ISO
Config.Description: Optional. Path to your own Windows ISO. When set, VERSION is ignored.

Config.Name: Unraid Docker settings
Config.Description: Read-only. Lets WinBox check that Unraid's Docker Stop Timeout is long enough for Windows to shut down cleanly, and warn in the log if not.

Config.Name: OEM folder
Config.Description: Optional. Folder copied to C:\OEM; an install.bat inside it runs at the end of setup (good for drivers like the GPU driver).

Config.Name: Windows version
Config.Description: 11 = Windows 11 Pro, 10 = Windows 10 Pro, 11l/10l = LTSC, 11e/10e = Enterprise, 2025/2022/2019 = Server.

Config.Name: Username
Config.Description: Windows account created during installation.

Config.Name: Password
Config.Description: Required. Password for the Windows account and the web console. Defaults like admin are refused.

Config.Name: Protect web console
Config.Description: Y = the web console on port 8006 asks for the username and password above.

Config.Name: Language
Config.Description: Windows language, for example English, German, French.

Config.Name: Product key
Config.Description: Optional. Your Windows product key.

Config.Name: RAM
Config.Description: Memory for Windows, for example 8G or 16G. Keep the --memory cap in Extra Parameters about 8G higher: the GPU memory window and the per-app GPU helpers live outside this.

Config.Name: CPU cores
Config.Description: Number of virtual CPU cores. Use the CPU Pinning setting below to keep Windows off the cores Unraid uses.

Config.Name: System disk size
Config.Description: Size of the Windows system disk. Can be increased later (then extend C: in Disk Management).

Config.Name: KVM
Config.Description: Hardware virtualization. Required.

Config.Name: TUN
Config.Description: Networking for the VM. Required.

Config.Name: GPU acceleration
Config.Description: Y = 3D acceleration on a GPU that Unraid and other containers keep using. Needs --runtime=nvidia (Nvidia) and --device=/dev/dri in Extra Parameters, and the Nvidia Driver plugin.

Config.Name: Virtual GPU type
Config.Description: virtio-vga-gl,neptune=true = Triton: Windows DirectX 11 runs on your GPU (needs the Triton driver in Windows, see README). virtio = display only. Without GPU acceleration a plain virtio display is used automatically.

Config.Name: Nvidia GPU UUID
Config.Description: UUID of the Nvidia GPU from Plugins > Nvidia Driver (starts with GPU-), or 'all'. The same GPU can be given to Plex, Jellyfin and others.

Config.Name: Nvidia capabilities
Config.Description: Must include graphics and display. Leave at 'all'.

Config.Name: GPU memory budget
Config.Description: Video memory Windows may use on the shared GPU, as a power of two (2G, 4G, 8G). Leave room for the other containers.

Config.Name: Render node
Config.Description: Optional. Picked automatically, preferring the Nvidia card. Set it, for example /dev/dri/renderD128, to choose a specific GPU.

Config.Name: Moonlight streaming
Config.Description: Y = Sunshine in the container streams Windows to Moonlight, with the video encoded on the shared NVIDIA GPU (NVENC) instead of on Windows' CPU cores. Needs GPU acceleration = Y. Pair Moonlight in Sunshine's web UI (port 47990, same login as the web console). Don't also run Sunshine inside Windows.

Config.Name: Sunshine web UI
Config.Description: Sunshine's settings page, for pairing Moonlight: https://[unraid-ip]:47990

Config.Name: Sunshine HTTPS
Config.Description: Moonlight streaming (pairing and control).

Config.Name: Sunshine HTTP
Config.Description: Moonlight streaming (finding the host).

Config.Name: Sunshine RTSP
Config.Description: Moonlight streaming (session setup).

Config.Name: Sunshine video
Config.Description: Moonlight streaming (video).

Config.Name: Sunshine control
Config.Description: Moonlight streaming (control).

Config.Name: Sunshine audio
Config.Description: Moonlight streaming (audio).

Config.Name: GPU passthrough
Config.Description: Alternative to shared mode: the GPU is taken away from Unraid and every other container while Windows runs. Set GPU acceleration to N. PCI address from Tools > System Devices, for example 01:00.0. The GPU's audio function is added automatically. Bind it to VFIO first, then add --device=/dev/vfio/vfio --device=/dev/vfio/N (N = its IOMMU group) to Extra Parameters.

Config.Name: GPU is primary display
Config.Description: Y = Windows uses only the passed-through GPU (plug a monitor or dummy plug into it). Turns off the web console; use RDP, Parsec or Sunshine. N = keep the web console as a second display.

Config.Name: GPU vBIOS ROM
Config.Description: Optional. Path inside the container to a vBIOS ROM file. Only needed for cards that fail to start, usually the GPU Unraid booted from. Map the file with 'GPU ROM file' below and enter /roms/gpu.rom here.

Config.Name: GPU ROM file
Config.Description: Optional. The vBIOS file on Unraid, for example /mnt/user/isos/vbios/gpu.rom.

Config.Name: Other PCI passthrough
Config.Description: Optional. More vfio-bound PCI devices, comma separated, for example a USB controller 03:00.0 or an NVMe drive. Add --device=/dev/vfio/N for each extra IOMMU group.

Config.Name: Pass whole IOMMU group
Config.Description: Y = automatically add the other devices that share an IOMMU group with the ones you listed (bridges excluded). VFIO needs the whole group.

Config.Name: USB passthrough
Config.Description: Optional. USB devices as vendor:product, comma separated, for example 046d:c52b (run 'lsusb' on the Unraid terminal). Add --device=/dev/bus/usb to Extra Parameters. Connect USB drives only after Windows is installed.

Config.Name: Sound
Config.Description: Y = Windows' sound plays in the web console, and in Moonlight with streaming on. N = no sound in either.

Config.Name: Extra QEMU arguments
Config.Description: Optional raw QEMU arguments, for experts.
